override.repo_standard: decision:own-helper-not-anchors-helper, graded @grade: settled/human, leans g1 — an inbound map anchor on this gate's handoff. Under the decision-fixedness doctrine in references/global-everyone.md, settled/human means an executor may not unsettle it locally; it must be floated to the tier that ruled it.
override.reason: The decision subordinates the smell twice over. Substantively, the two fields' live shapes genuinely differ — anchors carries dict->[str] | dict->str | [str], directives carries dict->dict | [str] — so a shared normalizer would have to branch on both anyway and would deepen coupling rather than remove duplication; the anchors helper flattens to one line per leaf, which would destroy the nested contract indentation directives needs. Procedurally, the tier is settled/human, so consolidating here would be an unsanctioned unsettling by a reviewer, not a cleanup.

Present in the literal sense: the directive contract is an untyped nested dict discriminated at runtime by isinstance rather than modelled as a Directive value object with a spelling method.

override.reason: The state file is the interface here, so a value object would be a wrapper the engine must serialize back to the same primitives at every boundary — added interface for no added behaviour, and a departure from the uniform posture of every other field in the file. global-everyone's 'one canonical path; no speculative abstraction' points the same way. Introducing the type for one renderer would also be exactly the speculative generality flagged below.

The else branch at lines 1716-1717 — a dict whose value is not itself a dict, rendered as one leaf line beside its name — handles a shape that does not exist in the corpus. The implementer says so plainly in its own result ('Not a corpus shape - a defensive branch'), and no test exercises it. I proved it is dead with respect to the suite by mutation: replacing that line with an unconditional raise leaves the full file at '346 passed, 30 subtests passed', EXIT=0. So it is untested generality shipped for a hypothetical input. NON-BLOCKING and I am not asking for it to be removed at this gate: it is two lines, it is honestly documented as defensive, and without it a {name: scalar} value would emit a bare '  name:' header with nothing under it, which is worse than the branch under the fail-visibly rule. The finding is that it should be either covered by a test or dropped, and that a defensive branch nothing can reach is indistinguishable from one that works. Routed as an observation to Commander, not a blocker.

The ratio is striking: a 19-line docstring over 12 executable lines in _render_directive_lines, a 7-line docstring over 5 in _directive_leaf, and a 6-line comment over a 1-line change in state(). On its face that is comment compensating for code.
